components.note: 刂 (knife) — peeling is done with a blade or the fingers acting like one.
录 (lù) gives a sound distantly related to bō, having drifted apart over time.
大 (a person, arms spread wide) — depicts someone in the act of grabbing.
寸 (a hand) — grasping at something, together giving 夺 its meaning 'to seize, take by force.'

example.hanzi: 独裁政府剥夺了公民的言论自由。
example.pinyin: dúcái zhèngfǔ bōduóle gōngmín de yánlùn zìyóu.
example.english: The dictatorial government deprived citizens of their freedom of speech.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948, explicitly protects freedom of expression in Article 19. Yet press-freedom watchdogs have found that in the decades since, more governments have restricted that freedom than expanded it, often through censorship, licensing controls, or outright bans on independent media.

meanings: (fig.) to spend money in large amounts

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl
丿 — a single drop of blood inside the vessel

example.hanzi: 他摔倒后手臂出血了。
example.pinyin: tā shuāidǎo hòu shǒubì chūxuèle.
example.english: He bled from his arm after he fell.
example.fact: The human body holds roughly five liters of blood, and a healthy adult can safely donate about half a liter at a time. The lost plasma volume is typically replaced within about 48 hours, though the red blood cells themselves take several weeks to fully regenerate.

components.note: 寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 他的导师建议他申请那份奖学金。
example.pinyin: tā de dǎoshī jiànyì tā shēnqǐng nà fèn jiǎngxuéjīn.
example.english: His advisor suggested that he apply for that scholarship.
example.fact: The English word 'mentor' comes from Mentor, a character in Homer's Odyssey whom Odysseus entrusted to guide his son Telemachus. The term entered English usage in the 18th century and now describes any experienced advisor who guides someone less experienced.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a figure that stands tall above the rest, like a tree rising over a forest, giving 杰 its meaning 'outstanding, heroic.'
灬 (fire, shown as four dots) — traditionally tied to brilliance or radiance, reinforcing the sense of someone who shines above others.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 这部电影被誉为导演的杰作。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng bèi yùwéi dǎoyǎn de jiézuò.
example.english: This film is regarded as the director's masterpiece.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci is believed to have worked on the Mona Lisa intermittently for about 16 years and reportedly kept it with him until his death in 1519. It now hangs in the Louvre behind bulletproof glass and is viewed by millions of visitors every year.

meanings: sign (that sth is about to happen)

components.note: 彳 (a step/road) — 征 relates to a long journey or military campaign
正 (zhèng) gives a sound close to 征's reading zhēng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
兆 is traditionally read as a picture of the cracks that appear in a heated tortoise shell or bone, used by ancient diviners to predict the future — the source of its meaning 'omen.'

example.hanzi: 头痛有时是感冒的征兆。
example.pinyin: tóutòng yǒushí shì gǎnmào de zhēngzhào.
example.english: A headache is sometimes a sign of catching a cold.
example.fact: Seismologists have observed small tremors, shifts in groundwater levels, and unusual animal behavior before some major earthquakes, but no such signal has proven reliable enough to predict exactly when or where a quake will strike, which is why earthquake prediction remains largely impossible today.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
羽 (feather) — 翁 originally referred to the neck feathers of a bird.
公 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to 翁's reading wēng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他年轻时就成了百万富翁。
example.pinyin: tā niánqīng shí jiù chéngle bǎiwàn fùwēng.
example.english: He became a millionaire while he was still young.
example.fact: John D. Rockefeller, often cited as history's first documented billionaire, built his fortune through the Standard Oil Company in the late 19th century. Adjusted for inflation, his peak net worth is estimated to have exceeded $300 billion in today's dollars.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
亻 (person) — 例 relates to an example or precedent set by a particular case
列 (liè) gives a sound close to 例's reading lì, sharing the same initial consonant and tone

example.hanzi: 这家医院上个月收治了三十个新冠病例。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā yīyuàn shàng gè yuè shōuzhìle sānshí gè xīnguān bìnglì.
example.english: This hospital admitted thirty COVID-19 cases last month.
example.fact: John Snow's 1854 map plotting cholera cases in London around a single water pump is considered a founding moment of modern epidemiology. His analysis identified the pump as the outbreak's source well before germ theory was widely accepted by the medical establishment.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 销 originally meant to melt metal.
肖 (xiào) gives a rhyme close to xiāo, with the tone shifted.
臼 pictures a clay mortar or vessel.
殳 (a tool, held in a hand) strikes it, giving 毁 its meaning 'to destroy, to smash.'

example.hanzi: 警方销毁了缴获的毒品。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng xiāohuǐle jiǎohuò de dúpǐn.
example.english: The police destroyed the confiscated drugs.
example.fact: Central banks routinely shred and destroy old, damaged banknotes withdrawn from circulation. The U.S. Federal Reserve destroys millions of dollars in worn-out bills every day, replacing them with newly printed currency of equal value.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饥 describes the lack of food, hunger.
几 (jǐ) gives the sound — close to jī, differing only in tone.
饣 (food) — 饿 relates to a need for food.
我 (I, self) suggests personal want or need — paired with food, giving 饿 its meaning 'hungry.'

example.hanzi: 战争导致了大规模的饥饿。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng dǎozhìle dà guīmó de jī'è.
example.english: The war led to widespread famine.
example.fact: The Irish Potato Famine of the 1840s, triggered by a potato blight fungus, is estimated to have caused around one million deaths and drove more than a million people to emigrate, permanently reshaping Ireland's population and its diaspora across North America.

components.note: 女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'

example.hanzi: 别担心,这不要紧。
example.pinyin: bié dānxīn, zhè bù yàojǐn.
example.english: Don't worry, it's not important.
example.fact: Survival rates for cardiac arrest drop by roughly 10 percent for every minute that passes without CPR or defibrillation, which is why paramedics refer to the first several minutes after a person collapses as the critical window for intervention.

meanings: variant of 陽臺|阳台[yang2 tai2]

components.note: 阝 (a hillside/place) — the sunlit side of a hill or place
日 (the sun) — the source of light and warmth
台 originally depicted a raised mound or earthen platform, a simple structure standing above the surrounding ground — the source of its meaning 'platform, stage, terrace.'

example.hanzi: 我喜欢在阳台上种花。
example.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan zài yángtái shàng zhòng huā.
example.english: I like growing flowers on the balcony.
example.fact: The English word 'balcony' entered the language from Italian balcone, ultimately traced to a Germanic word for a beam or piece of scaffolding. Balconies became a defining feature of Italian Renaissance architecture before spreading across the rest of Europe.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 这只是我的一点心意,请收下。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǐshì wǒ de yìdiǎn xīnyì, qǐng shōuxià.
example.english: This is just a small token of my regard — please accept it.
example.fact: In many East Asian cultures, gifts for weddings and New Year celebrations are traditionally wrapped in red paper, since red is associated with luck and prosperity, while white wrapping is generally avoided because of its association with mourning.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
禾 (grain) — 称 originally referred to weighing grain on a balance scale, a sense that extended over time to 'to assess' and then 'to call, to name.'
尔 is close in sound to chēng, standing in as the historical phonetic element even though the two readings have drifted apart.

example.hanzi: 他自称是这家公司的创始人。
example.pinyin: tā zìchēng shì zhè jiā gōngsī de chuàngshǐrén.
example.english: He claims to be the founder of this company.
example.fact: Anna Anderson was one of several women who, over several decades, claimed to be Grand Duchess Anastasia, the youngest daughter of Russia's last tsar, believed killed with her family in 1918. DNA testing conducted in the 1990s proved that Anderson was unrelated to the Romanov family.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.

example.hanzi: 哈罗德是我在伦敦认识的朋友。
example.pinyin: Hāluódé shì wǒ zài Lúndūn rènshi de péngyou.
example.english: Harold is a friend I met in London.
example.fact: Harrods, the London department store whose name derives from founder Charles Henry Harrod, opened as a small grocery shop in 1834 and grew into one of the world's largest department stores, spanning more than a million square feet across five floors.

components.note: 画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.
画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.

example.hanzi: 我妹妹喜欢画画。
example.pinyin: wǒ mèimei xǐhuan huàhuà.
example.english: My younger sister likes to draw.
example.fact: The Cave of Altamira in Spain contains paintings of bison and other animals created more than 14,000 years ago using natural pigments such as ochre and charcoal. Discovered in 1868, it is sometimes called the 'Sistine Chapel of Paleolithic art.'

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.

example.hanzi: 那座火山已经沉睡了两百年。
example.pinyin: nà zuò huǒshān yǐjīng chénshuìle liǎng bǎi nián.
example.english: That volcano has been dormant for two hundred years.
example.fact: Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption in Indonesia was the most powerful in recorded history, ejecting so much ash and sulfur into the atmosphere that it cooled global temperatures and made 1816 known as the 'Year Without a Summer' across Europe and North America.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他把这个问题反映给了上级。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zhège wèntí fǎnyìng gěile shàngjí.
example.english: He reported the problem to his superiors.
example.fact: Stanley Milgram's 1961 obedience experiments at Yale found that a majority of participants were willing to administer what they believed were painful electric shocks to a stranger simply because an authority figure in a lab coat instructed them to keep going.

components.note: The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.
亻 (person) on the left represents someone tending to something small.
子 (child) on the right depicts the small, young thing being watched over, giving 仔 its meaning of something small or young.
衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.

example.hanzi: 他穿着一条蓝色的牛仔裤。
example.pinyin: tā chuānzhe yī tiáo lán sè de niúzǎikù.
example.english: He is wearing a pair of blue jeans.
example.fact: Levi Strauss and tailor Jacob Davis patented the use of copper rivets to reinforce denim work pants in 1873, creating the modern blue jean. The rivets were placed at stress points like pocket corners to keep the pants from tearing during hard labor.

components.note: 氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'
Woman — an old semantic root sometimes linked to feelings.
Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他涉嫌参与了这起诈骗案。
example.pinyin: tā shèxián cānyùle zhè qǐ zhàpiàn àn.
example.english: He is suspected of being involved in this fraud case.
example.fact: The term 'Ponzi scheme' comes from Charles Ponzi, who defrauded investors in Boston in 1920 by promising 50 percent returns within 45 days. He paid earlier investors with money collected from new ones until the scheme collapsed within about a year.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逃 means to escape or flee, involving movement.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to táo, with the initial shifted.
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 警方悬赏抓捕那名逃犯。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng xuánshǎng zhuōbǔ nà míng táofàn.
example.english: The police offered a reward for capturing that fugitive.
example.fact: D. B. Cooper hijacked a Boeing 727 in 1971, extorted $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted from the plane over the Pacific Northwest. Despite one of the longest manhunts in FBI history, he was never identified or found.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 财's reading cái
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 政 relates to administering or governing.
正 (zhèng) gives the sound — 政 is also pronounced zhèng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 政府正在讨论明年的财政预算。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ zhèngzài tǎolùn míngnián de cáizhèng yùsuàn.
example.english: The government is discussing next year's fiscal budget.
example.fact: The Bank of England, founded in 1694 to help fund a war against France, is considered one of the first institutions to formalize modern government deficit financing by selling long-term bonds to the public.

components.note: 冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.
土 (earth/soil) — 块 originally referred to a lump or clod of earth
夬 (guài) gives a sound distantly related to 块's reading kuài, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 请在我的饮料里加些冰块。
example.pinyin: qǐng zài wǒ de yǐnliào lǐ jiā xiē bīngkuài.
example.english: Please add some ice cubes to my drink.
example.fact: Before mechanical refrigeration became common in the 20th century, 19th-century entrepreneurs such as Frederic Tudor built a global 'ice trade,' cutting blocks of ice from frozen New England ponds and shipping them by sea as far as India and the Caribbean.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 依 relates to a person relying or leaning on something
衣 (yī) gives the sound — 依 is also pronounced yī, an exact match
丨 is a simple vertical stroke, a marker element in this character's form.
日 (sun, day) — 旧 relates to the passage of many days, giving it the meaning 'old, former.'

example.hanzi: 多年过去了,他依旧住在那个小镇。
example.pinyin: duō nián guòqùle, tā yījiù zhù zài nàge xiǎozhèn.
example.english: Many years have passed, and he still lives in that small town.
example.fact: General Sherman, a giant sequoia in California's Sequoia National Park, is estimated to be around 2,200 years old and remains the largest known tree on Earth by volume, having grown slowly but steadily for millennia.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'
者 originally pictured ash sifting through a container, an image later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated grammatical word meaning 'the one who' or 'the person that.'

example.hanzi: 那位使者带来了国王的口信。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shǐzhě dàiláile guówáng de kǒuxìn.
example.english: That envoy brought a message from the king.
example.fact: According to legend, the Greek messenger Pheidippides ran roughly 40 kilometers from the battlefield of Marathon to Athens in 490 BC to announce a Greek victory over Persia, collapsing after delivering the news. The modern marathon race is named after his run.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — work involving livestock, done imperfectly
工 (work) — the labor itself, linked to the idea of falling short
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 这两种材料的价格有很大差别。
example.pinyin: zhè liǎng zhǒng cáiliào de jiàgé yǒu hěn dà chābié.
example.english: There is a big price difference between these two materials.
example.fact: Identical twins share nearly all of their DNA at birth, yet studies show that environmental and epigenetic differences accumulate over a lifetime, causing their gene expression patterns to diverge more and more as they age even though their genomes remain the same.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — suggests departing or leaving.
贵 (valuable, precious) — leaving something valuable behind gave 遗 its meaning 'to lose, to leave behind.'
亠厶-shaped top pictures a bundled object being cast away.
廾 (two hands) below shows the act of throwing it out, giving 弃 its meaning 'to abandon, discard.'

example.hanzi: 这只小狗被主人遗弃在路边。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu bèi zhǔrén yíqì zài lùbiān.
example.english: This little dog was abandoned by its owner on the roadside.
example.fact: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone in Ukraine has been largely abandoned by humans since the 1986 nuclear disaster, yet wildlife populations there — including wolves, lynx, and wild horses — have rebounded in the decades since, thriving in the absence of human activity.

components.note: 缶 (a clay jar) — 缺 relates to something broken or missing, like a cracked vessel.
夬 (guài) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading quē has diverged.
阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'

example.hanzi: 这批产品被发现存在设计缺陷。
example.pinyin: zhè pī chǎnpǐn bèi fāxiàn cúnzài shèjì quēxiàn.
example.english: This batch of products was found to have a design defect.
example.fact: The original Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington state collapsed in 1940, just months after opening, when wind-induced oscillations exposed a fatal flaw in its slender, flexible deck. The disaster reshaped modern bridge engineering and aerodynamic testing.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这支军队拥有强大的火力。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī jūnduì yǒngyǒu qiángdà de huǒlì.
example.english: This army possesses powerful firepower.
example.fact: The Gatling gun, patented in 1862, is often cited as one of the first practical rapid-fire weapons, capable of firing several hundred rounds per minute. It foreshadowed the machine guns that would come to dominate 20th-century warfare.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.
月 is a simple picture of a crescent moon.

example.hanzi: 上个月我们去北京旅游了。
example.pinyin: shàng gè yuè wǒmen qù Běijīng lǚyóule.
example.english: Last month we traveled to Beijing.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 to correct drift in the older Julian calendar, is the calendar most widely used today. Some countries, notably Russia, did not adopt it until the 20th century.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
退 (to step back, retreat) — used to move and walk, together giving 腿 its meaning 'leg.'

example.hanzi: 早餐我常常吃火腿三明治。
example.pinyin: zǎocān wǒ chángcháng chī huǒtuǐ sānmíngzhì.
example.english: For breakfast I often eat a ham sandwich.
example.fact: Parma ham, or prosciutto di Parma, must by Italian law be cured for at least 12 months using only salt and time, with no nitrates or other preservatives permitted under its protected designation of origin.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
止 depicts a footprint, with toes at the top and the leg below — a simple picture of a foot, later extended to mean 'to stop.'

example.hanzi: 警察及时制止了这场斗殴。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá jíshí zhìzhǐle zhè chǎng dòu'ōu.
example.english: The police stopped the fight in time.
example.fact: Stock exchanges use automatic 'circuit breakers' that halt trading for a set period if a major index falls by a certain percentage in a single day. The mechanism was introduced in the United States after the 1987 Black Monday crash to curb panic selling.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 经过多年战乱,这个国家终于恢复了安定。
example.pinyin: jīngguò duōnián zhànluàn, zhège guójiā zhōngyú huīfùle āndìng.
example.english: After years of war, the country finally regained stability.
example.fact: A spinning gyroscope resists changes to its orientation because of a property called conservation of angular momentum. The same principle helps keep a moving bicycle upright and is used to stabilize spacecraft, ships, and camera rigs.

components.note: 贝 (currency, wealth) sits on the left.
戋 means 'small, little' — paired with money 贝, this pictures something costing very little, giving 贱 its meaning 'cheap, of low value.'
贝 (shell/money) — 货 relates to goods that are bought and sold for money
化 (huà) gives a sound distantly related to 货's reading huò, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 她在小说里骂那个反派"贱货"。
example.pinyin: tā zài xiǎoshuō lǐ mà nàge fǎnpài "jiànhuò".
example.english: In the novel, she calls the villain a "jiànhuò."
example.fact: For centuries, various legal systems classified enslaved people as property rather than persons, a practice not formally abolished in the last country to do so, Mauritania, until 1981. Estimates today suggest tens of millions of people worldwide remain trapped in forms of forced labor.

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
钅 (metal) shows 锁 is typically a metal object.
⺌ (a form of 小) gives a sound distantly related to suǒ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们换了新的门锁。
example.pinyin: wǒmen huànle xīn de ménsuǒ.
example.english: We changed to a new door lock.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians developed the earliest known pin-lock mechanism around 4,000 years ago, made from wood. The same basic pin-tumbler principle, later refined by Linus Yale Jr. in the 1860s, is still used in most standard door locks today.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.hanzi: 那个小伙很有礼貌。
example.pinyin: nàge xiǎohuǒ hěn yǒu lǐmào.
example.english: That young guy is very polite.
example.fact: In Japan, Coming of Age Day (Seijin no Hi) is a national holiday held on the second Monday of January, celebrating everyone who turned 20 during the previous year. Many young women mark the occasion by wearing an elaborate furisode kimono.

meanings: an exciting turn of events (to watch unfold)

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'

example.hanzi: 好戏还在后头呢。
example.pinyin: hǎoxì hái zài hòutou ne.
example.english: The best part of the show is still to come.
example.fact: London's Globe Theatre, where many of Shakespeare's plays premiered starting in 1599, could hold up to 3,000 spectators standing in the open-air yard around the stage. The original building burned down in 1613 after a stage cannon ignited its thatched roof.

components.note: 后 originally pictured a ruler issuing commands and came to mean 'empress, queen.' When Chinese characters were simplified, this ancient form was also adopted to write the unrelated word 后 'behind, back,' replacing the more complex traditional character 後.
⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body
北 (běi) gives a sound close to 背's reading bèi, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他的后背被太阳晒得又红又痛。
example.pinyin: tā de hòubèi bèi tàiyáng shàide yòu hóng yòu tòng.
example.english: His back was burned red and sore by the sun.
example.fact: The human spine has 33 vertebrae at birth, but several fuse together in the sacrum and coccyx by adulthood, leaving 26 movable bones. It is also naturally curved in an S-shape, which helps absorb shock while walking or running.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.

example.hanzi: 他的身高超过一米九。
example.pinyin: tā de shēngāo chāoguò yī mǐ jiǔ.
example.english: His height is over 1.9 meters.
example.fact: Robert Wadlow, the tallest man ever medically documented, reached 2.72 meters (8 feet 11 inches) before his death in 1940 at age 22. His extraordinary growth was caused by a pituitary gland disorder that led to excessive growth hormone production.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'

example.hanzi: 一位老太太正在公园里散步。
example.pinyin: yī wèi lǎotàitai zhèngzài gōngyuán lǐ sànbù.
example.english: An elderly lady is taking a walk in the park.
example.fact: Jeanne Calment of France holds the verified record for the longest confirmed human lifespan, living to 122 years and 164 days before her death in 1997. Her record has stood for decades despite continued advances in healthcare and life expectancy.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — the payment involved.
卖 (to sell) — combined with money, the image of buying something back, giving 赎 its meaning 'to redeem, ransom.'
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.hanzi: 绑匪要求支付一百万美元的赎金。
example.pinyin: bǎngfěi yāoqiú zhīfù yī bǎiwàn měiyuán de shújīn.
example.english: The kidnappers demanded a one-million-dollar ransom.
example.fact: King Richard the Lionheart of England was captured in 1192 while returning from the Crusades, and his release required a ransom of roughly 150,000 marks, an amount so large that England's treasury needed years of special taxation to raise it.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 最近的工作压力让他很心烦。
example.pinyin: zuìjìn de gōngzuò yālì ràng tā hěn xīnfán.
example.english: Recent work pressure has left him feeling very agitated.
example.fact: Chronic stress triggers sustained release of cortisol, a hormone that helps the body respond to short-term danger but, when elevated for long periods, has been linked to impaired memory, weakened immune function, and increased cardiovascular risk.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 宪法保障公民的言论自由。
example.pinyin: xiànfǎ bǎozhàng gōngmín de yánlùn zìyóu.
example.english: The constitution guarantees citizens' freedom of speech.
example.fact: The First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, ratified in 1791, prohibits Congress from abridging freedom of speech. The amendment restrains government action specifically, a distinction that leaves private companies and employers free to set their own speech rules.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.
讠 (speech) — relates to 该's meaning 'ought to, should,' as if reached through spoken agreement.
亥 (hài) gives a sound hint — 该 is pronounced gāi, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 他自己不小心摔倒了,活该。
example.pinyin: tā zìjǐ bù xiǎoxīn shuāidǎole, huógāi.
example.english: He fell because of his own carelessness — serves him right.
example.fact: Schadenfreude, the pleasure derived from another person's misfortune, has been studied by psychologists as a distinct emotion tied to envy or a sense of justice. Brain-imaging studies show it activates reward centers similar to those triggered by personal achievement.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 简 originally referred to bamboo strips used for writing
间 (jiān) gives a sound close to 简's reading jiǎn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
厤 (relating to the sequence of time) — 历 relates to history and the calendar
力 (lì) gives the sound — 历 is pronounced lì, an exact match

example.hanzi: 我正在修改我的简历。
example.pinyin: wǒ zhèngzài xiūgǎi wǒ de jiǎnlì.
example.english: I am revising my résumé.
example.fact: The résumé is sometimes traced back to Leonardo da Vinci, who in 1482 wrote a letter listing his skills and accomplishments to seek employment with the Duke of Milan, though the modern one-page résumé format did not become standard until the 20th century.

components.note: 禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'
氵 (water) — 润 describes something made moist or glossy by water.
闰 (rùn) gives the sound — an exact match with 润.

example.hanzi: 这家公司今年的利润大幅增长。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī jīnnián de lìrùn dàfú zēngzhǎng.
example.english: This company's profits have grown significantly this year.
example.fact: Standard Oil, founded by John D. Rockefeller in 1870, at its peak controlled about 90 percent of U.S. oil refining capacity. Its profits grew so large that the U.S. Supreme Court ordered the company broken into 34 separate firms in 1911 under antitrust law.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 恰 describes something that fits exactly as intended.
合 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to qià, having drifted apart over time.
尚 (esteemed, still) — carries a sense of something regarded as fitting or worthy.
田 (a field) — represents land of matching value, together giving 当 its meaning 'to correspond to, to be equivalent, appropriate.'

example.hanzi: 请选择一个恰当的词来填空。
example.pinyin: qǐng xuǎnzé yī gè qiàdàng de cí lái tiánkòng.
example.english: Please choose an appropriate word to fill in the blank.
example.fact: Astronomers use the term 'Goldilocks zone' to describe the range of distances from a star where a planet's temperature is just right for liquid water to exist on its surface — neither too hot nor too cold — a key factor in the search for potentially habitable exoplanets.

components.note: Hand — shows this is an action performed by hand.
Represents something being sent out or distributed.
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.

example.hanzi: 如果有紧急情况,请拨打这个电话号码。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ yǒu jǐnjí qíngkuàng, qǐng bōdǎ zhège diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: If there is an emergency, please dial this phone number.
example.fact: The 911 emergency number was first introduced in the United States in 1968, in Haleyville, Alabama, replacing a patchwork of local emergency numbers. It was chosen partly because it was short, easy to remember, and had not previously been used as an area code or service code.

components.note: 阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了受伤的部位。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiǎnchále shòushāng de bùwèi.
example.english: The doctor examined the injured part of the body.
example.fact: Proprioception, the sense of where your body parts are in space without looking, relies on specialized sensory receptors in muscles and joints called proprioceptors. It is what allows you to touch your nose with your eyes closed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 远处传来了阵阵歌声。
example.pinyin: yuǎnchù chuánláile zhènzhèn gēshēng.
example.english: Bursts of singing came drifting from a distance.
example.fact: Sound travels roughly four times faster through water than through air, at about 1,480 meters per second compared to 343 meters per second. This is why underwater listening devices called hydrophones can detect whale calls from many kilometers away.

meanings: Rus' (as in Kievan Rus' 基輔羅斯|基辅罗斯[Ji1 fu3 Luo2 si1])

components.note: 罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
斤 (an axe) — 斯 originally meant 'to split, to tear apart' with a blade, a sense that survives faintly in its modern use as the connective word 'this, thus.'
其 is close in sound to sī, though the connection between the two readings has drifted with time.

example.hanzi: 罗斯是我们班上新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Luósī shì wǒmen bān shàng xīnlái de jiāohuàn shēng.
example.english: Ross is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: Kievan Rus' was a medieval federation of Slavic and Finnic peoples that emerged around the 9th century, centered on the city of Kyiv. Historians consider it the common ancestor of the modern nations of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus.
